data.name: Turkey
data.summary: Turkey taxes residents on worldwide income at progressive rates up to 40%. Borsa Istanbul shares: 0% withholding. Foreign shares, bonds and private company stakes: up to 40% on the gain (PPI-indexed); real estate held over five years and Turkish joint-stock shares held over two years are outside the charge. Half of Turkish dividends is exempt (about 20% effective); foreign dividends up to 40%. Inheritance tax 1–10% by band after a TRY 2.9m exemption per child (2026), but it reaches only Turkish-situs assets unless a Turkish citizen is involved. Gifts from parents 5–15%. No net wealth tax; a 'valuable housing tax' applies to homes over TRY 17.7m. Since 2026 (Law 7582) a new resident with no Turkish residence or tax liability in the prior three years gets a 20-year exemption on all foreign income and gains (no remittance condition) and a flat 1% inheritance rate.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence (full taxpayer)
regimes.description: Full taxpayer on worldwide income; progressive rates 15–40%.
regimes.eligibility: Legal residence (domicile) in Turkey, or foreigners staying more than six months in a calendar year. Foreigners need a residence permit.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on Borsa Istanbul shares bought after 1 Jan 2006 and sold through a Turkish bank or broker fall under Temporary Article 67 withholding at 0% (final). Other gains are 'değer artışı kazancı' under GVK Mük. Art. 80 and are declared at the progressive rates (top 40%): this covers foreign shares and bonds, shares in limited companies (ortaklık payları), and shares of Turkish joint-stock companies held two years or less. Shares of Turkish joint-stock companies (tam mükellef kurumlar) held more than two years are outside the charge (Mük. 80/1). Real estate is taxed only if sold within five years of acquisition (Mük. 80/6). The cost is indexed by the producer price index when the increase is at least 10% (Mük. 81).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Annual exemption of TRY 150,000 (2026) for capital gains other than on securities (Mük. 80, amount set by GVK General Communiqué 332); it does not apply to securities gains. Real estate held more than five years and Turkish A.Ş. shares held more than two years are outside the charge.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Gains on securities traded abroad are not covered by the Temporary Article 67 withholding regime in this reading and are self-declared; whether foreign shares held through a Turkish bank fall under Art. 67 was not confirmed.

open_questions: Whether gains on foreign listed shares held through a Turkish intermediary fall under the Temporary Art. 67 withholding (15%/0%) rather than annual declaration was not confirmed; the JSON uses the declaration route at 40%.
Producer-price indexation (Mük. 81) lowers the effective rate on long-held assets in a high-inflation economy; the JSON shows the statutory top rate.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Domestic listed shares 0% (Temporary Art. 67 rate for Borsa Istanbul equities). Foreign listed securities 40%: Mük. 80/1 taxes gains on securities other than shares of Turkish resident companies held over two years, at the top progressive rate of 40% (Art. 103), before PPI indexation. Private business sale 40%: assumes a foreign company or a Turkish limited company (Mük. 80/4); a Turkish A.Ş. stake held over two years would be 0%. Real estate (Turkish or foreign) 0% when held more than five years (Mük. 80/6), otherwise up to 40%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Turkish A.Ş. shares: exempt after two years. Real estate: exempt after five years. No holding period for foreign securities.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Full taxpayers are taxed on worldwide income (GVK Art. 4), except under the Law 7582 new-resident exemption (Mük. 20/D).

dividends.summary: Half of gross dividends from Turkish companies is exempt; the rest is declared at progressive rates if over the TRY 400,000 (2026) threshold, with the 15% WHT (raised from 10% by Presidential Decision 9286, Dec 2024) creditable. Foreign dividends above TRY 22,000 (2026) must be declared and are taxed at progressive rates with a credit for foreign tax; the 50% exemption applies only to holdings of at least 50% remitted to Turkey.

wealth_tax.summary: No national net wealth tax. Ordinary property tax (0.1% residential, doubled in metropolitan areas) and a 'valuable housing tax' (0.3%–1.0% on the value above TRY 17,711,000 for 2026) apply to Turkish homes.

open_questions: The valuable housing tax is arguably a limited wealth levy on high-value homes; it is recorded as property tax here because its 2026 band limits were not verified.

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax (Law 7338) is levied on the recipient. For 2026 each child (and the spouse) has an exemption of TRY 2,907,136 on an inheritance share (Art. 4(b), Communiqué 57). Inheritances are then taxed by band: 1% on the first TRY 3m, 3% on the next 7m, 5% on the next 15m, 7% on the next 30m, and 10% above TRY 55m (Art. 16). Gifts are taxed at 10–30% on the same bands, but gifts from parents to children pay half those rates (5–15%) after a TRY 66,935 exemption. Scope (Art. 1): property located in Turkey, and property anywhere belonging to or acquired by Turkish citizens. A non-Turkish family inheriting assets held abroad is therefore outside the tax; only Turkish-situs assets are taxed.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: 2026: TRY 2,907,136 per child/spouse share (TRY 5,817,845 for a spouse with no descendants); TRY 66,935 for gifts. Household goods and personal effects exempt. Foreign inheritance tax paid on the same assets is deductible.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Scope depends on citizenship and situs, not residence: Turkish-situs assets are always in scope; foreign-situs assets only when the deceased/donor or heir is a Turkish citizen. Art. 1(3): a foreign heir not domiciled in Turkey who acquires a Turkish citizen's foreign assets is not taxed.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Band limits and exemptions are revalued every year by the VUK revaluation rate (25.49% for 2026). Tax can be paid in six instalments over three years (May and November). Under Law 7582, inheritances from a person holding the Mük. 20/D exemption are taxed at a flat 1% during the 20-year period (see special regime).

inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts (ivazsız intikal) are taxed at 10/15/20/25/30% on the same bands after a TRY 66,935 exemption (2026). Gifts from parents, a spouse or children are taxed at half those rates, i.e. 5–15% (Art. 16(2)), still well above the inheritance scale.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Art. 1: property of Turkish citizens (wherever located) and property located in Turkey. Foreign assets of non-Turkish citizens passing to non-Turkish heirs are outside the tax.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Citizenship and situs based; residence alone does not bring foreign assets into scope.

regimes.name: New-resident foreign-income exemption (Law No. 7582)
regimes.description: GVK Mük. Art. 20/D (added by Law 7582, in force for individuals becoming resident from 1 Jan 2026): an individual with no Turkish residence and no Turkish tax liability in the three calendar years before becoming resident is exempt from income tax on all foreign-source income and gains for 20 years. Exempt income is not declared and no remittance condition applies. Inheritances from such a person during the 20 years are taxed at a flat 1% (VİVK Art. 16, para. added by Law 7582).
regimes.eligibility: Became resident in Turkey (domicile or more than six months' stay) on or after 1 Jan 2026; no Turkish domicile and no full or limited Turkish tax liability in the three preceding calendar years (prior liability only for Turkish rental, investment or capital-gains income does not disqualify; wages, business or professional income does). Citizenship is irrelevant. An exemption certificate (İstisna Belgesi) must be obtained from the tax office by the end of the year of becoming resident (end of February of the next year if resident in the last two months). Individuals only; companies cannot use it.

capital_gains.summary: All foreign-source gains (foreign securities, foreign company stakes, foreign real estate) are exempt for 20 years and not declared. Turkish-source gains follow the standard rules. No remittance condition: the exemption applies whether or not proceeds are brought into Turkey.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Requires the İstisna Belgesi; foreign taxes on exempt income cannot be credited and related expenses are not deductible. No remittance basis: foreign income is exempt whether or not it is remitted to Turkey.

income.name: Turkey

income_tax.summary: Progressive income tax with a 2026 top rate of 40% (15/20/27/35/40%); the employment-income table is used (35% from TRY 1.5 million; non-employment income reaches 35% already at TRY 1.0 million). Employees pay 14% social security plus 1% unemployment insurance up to TRY 297,270 a month; Bag-Kur self-employed premium is 35.75% between a monthly floor and ceiling. Law 7582 gives individuals who become resident from 2026 a 20-year exemption on income obtained outside Turkey; per Tebliğ No. 333 it does not cover income from work or services performed in Turkey.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed (Bag-Kur, 4/1-b) premium 35.75% on earnings between TRY 1,101 a day (floor, TRY 11,808.23 a month premium) and TRY 9,909 a day (ceiling, TRY 106,274.03 a month premium). Cap shown is the annual earnings ceiling (9,909 x 360). Brackets above are the employment-income table (35% band from TRY 1.5 million). Free-lance (non-employment) income uses a different table in which the 27% band ends at TRY 1.0 million, adding up to TRY 40,000 of tax above TRY 1.5 million (PwC, opened 2026-10-15). A fixed filing fee of TRY 1,189.50 applies to taxpayers filing returns; salaried payroll pays 0.759% stamp tax.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income surtax. Employee social security (14%) is deductible from taxable income. The cap is the monthly ceiling TRY 297,270 x 12; the 1% unemployment insurance is paid by foreigners only if reciprocity exists.

regimes.name: New-resident exemption for foreign income (Law 7582, GVK 20/D)
regimes.description: Individuals who become Turkish residents on or after 1 January 2026, with no Turkish residence or tax liability in the preceding three calendar years, are exempt from income tax on income and earnings obtained outside Turkey for 20 years (GVK mukerrer art. 20/D, added by Law 7582 of 21 May 2026). Does not cover work done in Turkey: Income Tax General Communique No. 333 (Official Gazette 4 July 2026), art. 3(7), says only income obtained abroad is exempt and Turkish-source income stays taxable, and its Example 10 states that a freelance engineer working in Turkey and advising clients abroad earns self-employment income that is not exempt. A remote worker living and working in Turkey is therefore not covered for those fees or that salary (covers_local_work false). An exemption certificate must be obtained from the tax office by the end of the calendar year of becoming resident (by end of February of the next year if resident in the last two months).

succession.name: Turkey
succession.summary: Children, parents and a spouse have a protected share that a will cannot override (Civil Code arts. 505-506). A foreigner's estate follows their national law, except Turkish real estate, which follows Turkish law. Turkey has no trust law and family foundations are not allowed, and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants: one half of their statutory share; each parent: one quarter of theirs; the spouse: all of the statutory share when with descendants or parents, otherwise three quarters (Civil Code art. 506). Siblings' share was repealed in 2007. Free portion is the rest (art. 505).
succession.foreign_law_note: Law No. 5718 on Private International Law art. 20: succession follows the deceased's national law; immovables in Turkey follow Turkish law. A foreigner therefore keeps national law for movables only. Turkish courts may use public policy.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. Turkey has no trust law and does not clearly recognise a foreign trust. Foundations (vakif) are under Civil Code arts. 101-117 and the Foundations Law; the Code does not allow a foundation whose purpose is to support the founder's family. Foreign foundations are regulated separately.
open_questions: Confirm Law 5718 art. 20 text and the Foundations Law wording on family foundations (art. 101); I relied on knowledge.

immigration.name: Türkiye
immigration.summary: Türkiye is not in the EU, so EU, US and other passports use the same routes. Citizenship by investment starts at USD 400,000 in real estate (held 3 years) or USD 500,000 in a bank deposit, bonds, funds or fixed capital. A short-term residence permit by property needs USD 200,000. A digital nomad visa exists (about USD 3,000 a month, unconfirmed). Ordinary naturalisation is the fallback.
immigration.naturalisation: Ordinary naturalisation (Law No. 5901) is generally 5 years of residence plus language and conduct; not re-verified from the statute in this pass. Citizenship by investment by presidential decision needs no residence period.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Türkiye allows dual citizenship; the applicant's other country must allow it too (Global Citizen Solutions).

routes.name: Citizenship by investment - real estate (USD 400,000)
routes.summary: Buy property worth at least USD 400,000, keep it 3 years, and get a Turkish passport for yourself, spouse and children under 18.
routes.requirements: Exceptional citizenship by presidential decision (Law No. 5901): property worth at least USD 400,000, attested by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change; the title deed carries a no-sale restriction of at least 3 years and the buyer declares the purpose. Multiple properties can be combined. Applicant, spouse and children under 18 (or disabled children of any age) can be included; no residence or language requirement; clean record, no security concerns. Citizens of Armenia, Cuba, Nigeria, North Korea and Syria do not qualify (Global Citizen Solutions).
routes.investment_options: Other options start at USD 500,000 (see the following routes).
routes.physical_presence: None required; the applicant must visit once for biometrics (Global Citizen Solutions).
routes.family: Spouse and children under 18; parents get a residence permit only after citizenship.
routes.tax_note: Citizenship does not by itself create tax residence; residence is by 6 months' stay or domicile. A 2026 tax reform for new residents was reported by one source and is not verified.

routes.name: Long-term residence permit (indefinite)
routes.summary: After 8 years of continuous legal residence you can apply for an indefinite residence permit.
routes.requirements: Invest in Türkiye: at least 8 years of continuous residence, no social aid in the last 3 years, clean police record. Investors meeting the Council of Ministers' amounts (USD 400,000-500,000 options) may also get a 5-year permit and apply for long-term permit or citizenship.

routes.name: Digital Nomad Visa
routes.summary: A visa for remote workers employed or self-employed for clients abroad, reported at about USD 3,000 a month.
routes.requirements: Go Türkiye lists a Digital Nomad Identification Certificate and a pre-application, then a visa and short-term residence application at a Turkish mission. Secondary sources report income of about USD 3,000 a month (USD 36,000 a year), age 21-55 and a degree; eligible nationalities not confirmed (the consulate document lists countries including the US, UK, Germany). Official page did not show these figures.
routes.tax_note: A 2026 reform reported by one source gives qualified remote workers a deduction; not verified.

sources.title: Digital Nomads - Go Türkiye
sources.publisher: Türkiye Ministry of Culture and Tourism (Go Türkiye)

routes.name: Employer-sponsored work permit
routes.summary: Foreigners working in Türkiye need a work permit from the Ministry of Labor, applied for by the employer.
routes.requirements: Employer applies under the International Labour Force Law (No. 6735); quotas and salary floors apply. Residence is issued with the permit. Not researched in detail.
routes.tax_note: Resident taxpayers are taxed on worldwide income.

open_questions: Government fees for citizenship by investment: sourced figures come only from a consultancy (USD 400 application, USD 500 passport, USD 700 health cover); not given as fees here.
The invest.gov.tr guide is marked a test version; the Official Gazette text of the investment thresholds was not read.
Residence by property: USD 200,000 comes from law-firm reports of a migration directive (16 Oct 2023); the directive itself and the January 2025 appraisal change were not read.
Digital Nomad Visa: income, age, degree and eligible nationalities are not confirmed on an official page.
Ordinary naturalisation years and the 2026 tax reform for new residents were not verified.
